What is the flaw?', 'Signing may occur without approval.', 'Signing rules out approval.', 'The no statement has no conditional meaning.', 'Approved → signed. The author uses signed → approved without support.', 'Translate the no statement before judging its direction.'],\n+      ['A ↔ (B AND C). B is false. Therefore A is false. Is there a conditional flaw?', 'No. A requires B, so not B rules out A.', 'Yes. Any denial of a trigger is invalid.', 'Yes. C must also be false.', 'The A → (B AND C) direction makes B necessary. Denying B validly excludes A, regardless of C.', 'Inspect the necessary side of the biconditional.'],\n+    ],\n+  }),\n+  unit({ id: 'parallel', title: 'Match the argument’s structure', area: 'application', phase: 'conditional',\n+    prerequisites: ['flaw', 'de-morgan', 'domain'], goal: 'Match valid or flawed reasoning by form rather than by topic or word order.',\n+    teaching: ['Parallel reasoning compares how premises support a conclusion. “All approved plans are funded; P is approved; therefore P is funded” has the same form as “All trained ushers are assigned; U is trained; therefore U is assigned.” Different subjects do not change the move.', 'A chain between classes is different from applying a rule to a named case. A parallel flaw must preserve the mistaken direction. Match quantifiers, compound scope and conclusion strength. Reordered sentences or different positive wording can still express the same structure.'],\n+    method: ['Label the premises and conclusion.', 'Replace complete predicates with letters.', 'Identify the valid move or specific flaw.', 'Compare candidate forms, then verify wording and scope.'],\n+    workedExample: { statements: ['Every audited account has records.', 'Q has no records.', 'Therefore Q is not audited.'], reasoning: ['A → B; not B(Q); therefore not A(Q).', 'A matching argument must use the failed necessary condition to rule out its trigger.'], conclusion: 'Every blue pass is valid; T is invalid; therefore T is not blue is parallel.' },\n+    commonMistake: { mistake: 'Picking a candidate because it uses the same topic.', repair: 'Strip out the topic and match the inference, including whether it is valid or flawed.' },\n+    guided: ['Model: All A are B; X is B; therefore X is A. Which matches?', 'All artists sketch; Jo sketches; therefore Jo is an artist.', 'All artists sketch; Jo is an artist; therefore Jo sketches.', 'All artists sketch; Jo does not sketch; therefore Jo is not an artist.', 'The model affirms the necessary condition. Only the first argument repeats that flaw.', 'Match the direction of the move, not the letters’ meanings.'],\n+    practice: [\n+      ['Match A → B; A(x); therefore B(x).', 'All bakers rise early; Ana is a baker; therefore Ana rises early.', 'All bakers rise early; Ana rises early; therefore Ana is a baker.', 'All bakers rise early; Ana is not a baker; therefore Ana rises late.', 'The matching argument applies a rule forward to a qualifying individual.', 'Which fact supplies the sufficient condition?'],\n+      ['Match A → B; not B(x); therefore not A(x).', 'All open shops are staffed; this shop is unstaffed; therefore it is closed.', 'All open shops are staffed; this shop is closed; therefore it is unstaffed.', 'All open shops are staffed; this shop is staffed; therefore it is open.', 'The missing necessary result rules out the sufficient condition.', 'Find a valid contrapositive application.'],\n+      ['Match the flaw A → B; not A(x); therefore not B(x).', 'All members receive newsletters; Pat is not a member; therefore Pat receives none.', 'All members receive newsletters; Pat receives none; therefore Pat is not a member.', 'All members receive newsletters; Pat is a member; therefore Pat receives one.', 'The matching argument denies the sufficient condition and ignores other routes to B.', 'Match the specific error rather than any negative statement.'],\n+      ['Model: A → B and B → C; therefore A → C. Which matches the conclusion’s scope?', 'All divers swim; all swimmers train; therefore all divers train.', 'All divers swim; all swimmers train; Jo dives; therefore Jo trains.', 'All divers swim; Jo trains; therefore Jo dives.', 'The model concludes a class-to-class rule. The named-case argument adds a fact and a different conclusion form.', 'Distinguish a universal chain from applying that chain to a person.'],\n+      ['Model: (A AND B) → C; A(x); therefore C(x). Which repeats the flaw?', 'A licensed, insured driver qualifies; Jo is licensed; therefore Jo qualifies.', 'A licensed or insured driver qualifies; Jo is licensed; therefore Jo qualifies.', 'A licensed, insured driver qualifies; Jo has both; therefore Jo qualifies.', 'The model uses half a joint trigger as if it were enough.', 'Keep AND distinct from OR.'],\n+      ['Model: A → (B OR C); A(x); not B(x); therefore C(x). Which matches?', 'Members get a book or a voucher; Lee is a member without a book; therefore Lee gets a voucher.', 'Members get books and vouchers; Lee gets a voucher; therefore Lee is a member.', 'Members get books or vouchers; Lee gets a book; therefore Lee gets a voucher.', 'The same fact activates alternatives, and a negative fact removes one.', 'Look for an activated OR followed by elimination of one branch.'],\n+      ['Model: A → B; C → B; A(x); therefore C(x). Which repeats the flaw?', 'Painters and sculptors both train; Jo paints; therefore Jo sculpts.', 'Painters train; trainees sculpt; Jo paints; therefore Jo sculpts.', 'Painters train; Jo does not train; therefore Jo does not paint.', 'Two classes sharing a necessary property need not overlap in the named case.', 'The shared result is not a bridge between the triggers.'],\n+      ['Model: (A OR B) → C; not C(x); therefore not A(x) AND not B(x). Which matches?', 'A ticket or pass allows entry; Jo cannot enter; therefore Jo has neither.', 'A ticket and pass allow entry; Jo cannot enter; therefore Jo has neither.', 'A ticket or pass allows entry; Jo enters; therefore Jo has both.', 'Denying the consequence of an OR trigger excludes both alternative triggers.', 'Check both connector and direction.'],\n+      ['Model: All A are B; some C are A; therefore some C are B. Which matches?', 'All editors read; some musicians edit; therefore some musicians read.', 'All editors read; all musicians edit; therefore all musicians read.', 'Some editors read; some musicians edit; therefore some musicians read.', 'The matching structure carries an existing witness through a universal rule. The alternatives change the quantities or validity.', 'Preserve the existential witness and universal arrow.'],\n+    ],\n+  }),\n+  unit({ id: 'principle', title: 'Apply a rule without overstating a principle', area: 'application', phase: 'conditional',\n+    prerequisites: ['sufficient-assumption', 'mbt', 'domain'], goal: 'Check a rule’s complete trigger and distinguish rule application from general illustration.',\n+    teaching: ['Some principle tasks give a rule and ask which case it governs. “Any applicant with experience and a reference should be interviewed” requires both facts. An experienced applicant without a stated reference does not yet qualify.', 'Other principle tasks ask for an abstract idea illustrated by a case, rather than a strict conditional guarantee. First identify what the task asks. A single example does not establish a universal empirical law. A supplied normative rule can govern its stated cases without proving what actually happens.'],\n+    method: ['Identify whether the task asks application, justification or illustration.', 'For a rule, preserve its complete trigger and consequence.', 'For justification, test whether the principle bridges the facts to the conclusion.', 'For illustration, match the general idea without adding universal claims.'],\n+    workedExample: { statements: ['Policy: A late delivery caused by a documented outage should receive a refund.', 'Delivery J is late because of a documented outage.'], reasoning: ['Late AND caused by documented outage → should receive refund.', 'Both conditions are supplied for J.'], conclusion: 'J should receive a refund under the policy; actual payment is not established.' },\n+    commonMistake: { mistake: 'Treating any abstract sentence as a rigid trigger-and-consequence rule.', repair: 'Check the language and question demand. Illustration can require matching an idea rather than proving a formal implication.' },\n+    guided: ['Rule: Anyone trained and insured should lead the trip. Jo is trained. What extra fact completes this rule’s trigger?', 'Jo is insured.', 'Jo wants to lead.', 'Jo has led before.', 'The stated rule needs insurance in addition to training. Other attractive facts do not replace it.', 'Read every part before the rule’s consequence.'],\n+    practice: [\n+      ['Policy: Every verified claimant should receive a hearing. Which case clearly qualifies?', 'A claimant whose claim has been verified.', 'An unverified claimant who wants a hearing.', 'Someone who received a hearing but has no stated claim.', 'The verified-claimant trigger is explicitly satisfied.', 'Select the case with the stated sufficient condition.'],\n+      ['Rule: Projects without permits must pause. Project J has no permit. What follows?', 'J must pause under the rule.', 'J actually paused.', 'Every paused project lacks a permit.', 'The rule establishes an obligation for J, not actual behavior or the reverse rule.', 'Preserve must rather than changing it to did.'],\n+      ['Rule: A refund requires a receipt. Which fact rules out a refund under this rule?', 'The buyer has no receipt.', 'The buyer has a receipt.', 'The buyer asks for a refund.', 'No receipt denies the necessary condition. A receipt alone is not a guarantee.', 'Find the missing requirement.'],\n+      ['Policy: Trained and insured guides should be hired. Nora is insured; training is unknown. Is hiring required by this policy?', 'Not yet established.', 'Yes, insurance alone is enough.', 'The policy requires refusing Nora.', 'The complete joint trigger is not supplied. The policy also gives no refusal rule for nonqualifiers.', 'Check the unknown trigger component.'],\n+      ['Fact: A map is fragile. Conclusion: It should be stored flat. Which principle justifies this?', 'Fragile maps should be stored flat.', 'Maps stored flat are fragile.', 'Some fragile maps are stored flat.', 'The forward normative rule links this map’s fragility to the desired obligation.', 'Start with the supplied fact and end with should be stored flat.'],\n+      ['A club changed its schedule after listening to members. Which modest principle is illustrated?', 'Member feedback can guide organizational decisions.', 'Every organization always follows every member suggestion.', 'Only club members can make decisions.', 'The case illustrates responsiveness without supporting universal obedience or exclusivity.', 'Match the idea at the strength the example supports.'],\n+      ['Policy: Coastal projects with permits should receive inspections. J is coastal, permitted and already inspected. Which claim is warranted?', 'J meets the policy’s trigger.', 'Every inspected project is coastal and permitted.', 'J was inspected because of the policy.', 'J qualifies for the obligation. Actual inspection does not establish either reversal or its cause.', 'Separate qualifying under a rule from explaining behavior.'],\n+      ['Rule: A waived fee requires hardship or an administrative error. Fee F is waived and no error occurred. What follows under the rule?', 'Hardship applies to F.', 'Every hardship fee is waived.', 'F cannot have been waived.', 'Waiver requires one alternative. No error leaves hardship as necessary for F.', 'Use the OR requirement without reversing it.'],\n+      ['A mediator heard both parties before proposing a settlement. Which principle is illustrated without an unsupported guarantee?', 'Considering multiple perspectives can inform a proposal.', 'Hearing both parties always produces a successful settlement.', 'A settlement is impossible unless both parties agree with the mediator.', 'The conduct illustrates considering perspectives. Success and strict necessary conditions are not given.', 'Do not turn an illustration into a stronger causal or conditional law.'],\n+    ],\n+  }),\n*** End Patch"));

text(await tools.apply_patch("*** Begin Patch\n*** Update File: C:/Users/Joshu/dev/ai-os-projects/lsatu-conditional-bootcamp/src/bootcamps/conditionals/content/applications.source.ts\n@@\n       ['A mediator heard both parties before proposing a settlement. Which principle is illustrated without an unsupported guarantee?', 'Considering multiple perspectives can inform a proposal.', 'Hearing both parties always produces a successful settlement.', 'A settlement is impossible unless both parties agree with the mediator.', 'The conduct illustrates considering perspectives. Success and strict necessary conditions are not given.', 'Do not turn an illustration into a stronger causal or conditional law.'],\n     ],\n   }),\n+  unit({ id: 'quantifier-meaning', title: 'Read some, most and all precisely', area: 'quantifiers', phase: 'quantifier',\n+    prerequisites: ['whole-rule-negation', 'mbt'], goal: 'Distinguish existence, majority and universal membership.',\n+    teaching: ['Some means at least one. It permits one, several or all. Most means more than half of the stated population. All means every member satisfies the claim, but a universal statement alone does not establish that the population has members.', 'Keep the reference population fixed. Most musicians read does not say most readers are musicians. Some overlap is reversible: a person who is both a musician and a reader witnesses both statements. No means zero overlap. Many and few have no exact numerical cutoff without context.'],\n+    method: ['Name the reference population.', 'Translate some as at least one, most as more than half, all as every, and no as zero overlap.', 'Separate quantity from direction.', 'Avoid unstated percentages, existence and exclusivity.'],\n+    workedExample: { statements: ['Most of the ten volunteers have radios.'], reasoning: ['More than half of ten means at least six.', 'The volunteers are the reference group; radio owners may include many nonvolunteers.'], conclusion: 'At least six volunteers have radios. Most radio owners being volunteers is not established.' },\n+    commonMistake: { mistake: 'Reading some as some but not all.', repair: 'At least one permits all. A separate statement must exclude all.' },\n+    guided: ['Some editors are musicians. What follows?', 'At least one musician is an editor.', 'Most musicians are editors.', 'Some editors are not musicians.', 'The same overlapping person witnesses the reversed some statement. Neither majority nor a nonmusician is supplied.', 'Use one person in the overlap.'],\n+    practice: [\n+      ['Some maps are folded. Could every map be folded?', 'Yes.', 'No; some excludes all.', 'Only if most maps are not folded.', 'Some gives a lower bound of one, not an upper bound below all.', 'Ask whether some supplies an upper limit.'],\n+      ['Most of ten lockers are occupied. What is the minimum number occupied?', 'Six.', 'Five.', 'One.', 'Most requires strictly more than half. Half of ten is five.', 'Move above, not to, the halfway point.'],\n+      ['All lunar depots have radios. Must a lunar depot exist?', 'No.', 'Yes, at least one.', 'Yes, most depots are lunar.', 'The universal rule makes a claim about any qualifying depot without asserting a member.', 'Separate universal coverage from existence.'],\n+      ['Some painters are cooks. Which is equivalent?', 'Some cooks are painters.', 'Most cooks are painters.', 'All cooks are painters.', 'A single painter-cook is also a cook-painter. The quantity stays some.', 'Reverse the overlap without strengthening its size.'],\n+      ['Most astronomers read journals. Does it follow that most journal readers are astronomers?', 'No.', 'Yes.', 'No astronomer reads journals.', 'A majority within astronomers may be a tiny fraction of all readers.', 'Which population is the denominator in each statement?'],\n+      ['No registered boat lacks a radio. Which captures its meaning?', 'Every registered boat has a radio.', 'Every radio-equipped boat is registered.', 'Some registered boat lacks a radio.', 'Zero overlap between registered and radio-lacking makes radio necessary for registration.', 'Translate no as exclusion of the combined case.'],\n+      ['Most of seven panelists voted yes. What is the smallest yes count?', 'Four.', 'Three.', 'Six.', 'More than half of seven means more than three and a half, so four is the minimum.', 'Keep integer counts above the halfway point.'],\n+      ['Many residents cycle. Without additional context, what exact percentage is guaranteed by many?', 'No exact percentage.', 'More than fifty percent.', 'At least ninety percent.', 'Many is context-sensitive and is not automatically the quantifier most.', 'Do not substitute a numerical threshold for a vague quantity.'],\n+      ['All boats in an empty dry dock are inspected. Is that claim automatically contradicted by the dock being empty?', 'No; there is no uninspected boat there to violate it.', 'Yes; all always means at least one.', 'Yes; the claim requires a majority of boats.', 'A universal rule excludes counterexamples. An empty relevant set supplies none, but no existence claim follows.', 'Look for a violating member rather than assuming one exists.'],\n+    ],\n+  }),\n+  unit({ id: 'quantifier-negation', title: 'Deny quantities without overshooting', area: 'quantifiers', phase: 'quantifier',\n+    prerequisites: ['quantifier-meaning', 'whole-rule-negation'], goal: 'Negate all, some, none and most with exact strength.',\n+    teaching: ['Not all A are B means at least one A is not B. Not some A are B means no A are B. Not no A are B means some A are B. These are whole-statement denials, not swaps of the two groups.', 'Not most A are B means at most half of A are B. Exactly half is included. It does not always mean most A are not B. For ten members, a five-five split defeats most on both sides. With explicit finite counts, compute the boundary before choosing words.'],\n+    method: ['Identify the quantifier and reference population.', 'Ask what would make the complete claim false.', 'State the smallest exact denial.', 'Check half cases and avoid stronger none or majority claims.'],\n+    workedExample: { statements: ['Claim: Most of eight lamps are working.'], reasoning: ['The claim needs at least five working lamps.', 'Its denial permits zero through four working lamps.'], conclusion: 'At most four lamps are working denies the claim, including a four-four split.' },\n+    commonMistake: { mistake: 'Replacing not most with most not.', repair: 'Test an even split. It makes most false without making most not true.' },\n+    guided: ['Negate “Most of ten members attended.”', 'At most five attended.', 'At least six did not attend.', 'None attended.', 'Five attendees is enough to make most false. Requiring six absentees excludes that valid half case.', 'Include exactly half in the denial.'],\n+    practice: [\n+      ['Negate “All boxes are sealed.”', 'Some box is unsealed.', 'No box is sealed.', 'Most boxes are unsealed.', 'One counterexample defeats all; no or most would be unnecessarily stronger.', 'Find the smallest exception that defeats the rule.'],\n+      ['Negate “Some guides are licensed.”', 'No guide is licensed.', 'Some guide is unlicensed.', 'Not all guides are licensed.', 'The denial of at least one licensed guide is zero licensed guides.', 'Remove every witness to the existential claim.'],\n+      ['Negate “No tickets are refundable.”', 'Some ticket is refundable.', 'Every ticket is refundable.', 'Most tickets are refundable.', 'One refundable ticket defeats zero overlap.', 'How much overlap is needed to defeat none?'],\n+      ['Negate “Most of twelve windows are open.”', 'At most six are open.', 'At least seven are closed.', 'Exactly six are open.', 'Any count from zero through six defeats more than half. Exactly six is just one denying case.', 'Use a range that includes the halfway point.'],\n+      ['Negate “Some volunteers are not trained.”', 'Every volunteer is trained.', 'No volunteer is trained.', 'Some volunteer is trained.', 'Removing every untrained-volunteer witness means all volunteers meet training.', 'Negate both the quantity and the negative property.'],\n+      ['Negate “All residents have a card or a pass.”', 'Some resident has neither.', 'Some resident has no card but has a pass.', 'Every resident has neither.', 'A counterexample needs to fail both alternatives. The population remains residents.', 'Combine not-all with De Morgan.'],\n+      ['Most of nine chairs are occupied. Which exact negation applies?', 'At most four are occupied.', 'At most five are occupied.', 'Exactly four are occupied.', 'Five would satisfy most of nine. The denial allows zero through four.', 'Find the first majority count, then stop just below it.'],\n+      ['Claim: Most of ten accounts are active. Five are active and five inactive. What happens?', 'The claim and “most are inactive” are both false.', 'The claim is true.', 'Most are inactive is true.', 'Neither group exceeds half. This is why not most does not always become most not.', 'Compare each five-member group with more than five.'],\n+      ['Negate “Some licensed guides are insured and trained.”', 'No licensed guide has both insurance and training.', 'Every licensed guide is uninsured and untrained.', 'Some licensed guide is uninsured.', 'The denial removes the entire joint witness. Each licensed guide must lack insurance or training, but need not lack both.', 'Deny the existential conjunction as a whole.'],\n+    ],\n+  }),\n+  unit({ id: 'quantifier-linking', title: 'Carry witnesses and majorities through valid links', area: 'quantifiers', phase: 'quantifier',\n+    prerequisites: ['quantifier-meaning', 'quantifier-negation', 'direct-linking', 'domain'], goal: 'Identify valid some/all, most/all and same-population majority overlap.',\n+    teaching: ['Some A are B plus all B are C guarantees some A are C. The existing A-B witness travels through B → C. Most A are B plus all B are C guarantees most A are C, because every member of the majority also belongs to C.', 'If most of the same population are B and most of that same population are C, some of that population must be both. Two groups larger than half cannot be disjoint. Different reference populations do not create this overlap guarantee. The overlap need not itself be a majority.'],\n+    method: ['Mark the existing witness or majority and its reference population.', 'Follow only universal arrows from its established properties.', 'For two most statements, compare denominators.', 'State the weakest quantity the premises guarantee.'],\n+    workedExample: { statements: ['Most of ten guides have radios.', 'Most of those same ten guides have maps.'], reasoning: ['Each group contains at least six guides.', 'Two six-member groups inside ten must share at least two members.'], conclusion: 'Some guide has both a radio and a map; a majority with both is not guaranteed.' },\n+    commonMistake: { mistake: 'Linking any two statements containing most.', repair: 'Check whether the majorities share the same reference group, or whether a universal rule carries the first majority forward.' },\n+    guided: ['Some editors are swimmers. All swimmers are trained. What follows?', 'Some editors are trained.', 'All editors are trained.', 'Most trained people are editors.', 'An existing editor-swimmer is trained. No premise extends this to every editor.', 'Carry one witness through swimmers → trained.'],\n+    practice: [\n+      ['Some poets are teachers. All teachers read. What follows?', 'Some poets read.', 'All poets read.', 'No poet reads.', 'The poet-teacher witness is covered by teachers → readers.', 'Keep the quantity some while extending the property.'],\n+      ['Most boats are inspected. All inspected boats have radios. What follows?', 'Most boats have radios.', 'Most radio owners are boats.', 'All boats have radios.', 'Every member of the inspected majority carries into the radio group. The reference population remains boats.', 'Follow the majority through a universal arrow.'],\n+      ['Most of the same panel are lawyers; most are teachers. What follows?', 'Some panelist is both.', 'Most panelists are both.', 'No panelist is both.', 'Two majorities of one population must overlap, but the shared part can be smaller than half.', 'Test two six-member groups in a ten-member panel.'],\n+      ['Some volunteers are cooks. All cooks are insured. All insured people are listed. What follows?', 'Some volunteers are listed.', 'All volunteers are listed.', 'Most listed people volunteer.', 'The existing volunteer-cook follows both universal links.', 'Keep the same witness through the whole chain.'],\n+      ['Most of twelve students commute. Most of those same twelve work. What is the minimum overlap if each majority is as small as possible?', 'Two students.', 'Seven students.', 'Zero students.', 'Each majority has at least seven; fourteen memberships across twelve students requires at least two shared members.', 'Add the minimum group sizes and subtract the total population.'],\n+      ['Most bakers are readers. Most sculptors are readers. Must some baker be a sculptor?', 'No.', 'Yes, because both groups are majorities.', 'Yes, most bakers are sculptors.', 'The majorities have different reference populations. Their reader members could be disjoint.', 'Compare the denominators, not just the shared result word.'],\n+      ['Most guides are licensed. No licensed person is uninsured. What follows?', 'Most guides are insured.', 'Every guide is insured.', 'Most insured people are guides.', 'Licensed → insured carries the guide majority into insurance without reversing the reference group.', 'Translate the no statement into the universal arrow you can follow.'],\n+      ['Most of ten researchers are editors; most of those same ten are translators. All editors are trained. What follows?', 'Some researcher is a trained translator.', 'Most researchers are trained translators.', 'Every translator is a researcher.', 'The editor and translator majorities overlap. Every editor in that overlap is trained, so at least one trained translator exists.', 'First establish overlap, then carry its editor property through the universal rule.'],\n+      ['Some registered boats are rescue boats. Every rescue boat has a radio. Every registered radio-equipped boat is inspected. What follows?', 'Some registered boat is inspected.', 'Every registered boat is inspected.', 'Most inspected boats are rescue boats.', 'The existing registered-rescue witness gets a radio and satisfies both parts of the final restricted trigger.', 'Preserve registered status while adding radio status to the witness.'],\n+    ],\n+  }),\n+  unit({ id: 'quantifier-invalid', title: 'Recognize where quantity chains stop', area: 'quantifiers', phase: 'quantifier',\n+    prerequisites: ['quantifier-linking', 'flaw'], goal: 'Reject unsupported overlap, reversed majority and invalid most/some chains.',\n+    teaching: ['Some A are B and some B are C need not connect A to C. The two some statements may use different B members. All A are B plus some B are C also need not connect A to C: the B-C witness may be outside A.', 'Most A are B plus most B are C does not generally guarantee an A-C overlap. The second majority uses B as its population, which may include many non-A members. A universal arrow may carry an existing witness or majority; a partial overlap cannot replace that arrow. Build concrete countermodels to see why.'],\n+    method: ['Track which members each partial statement might describe.', 'Identify the population behind each most.', 'Try keeping relevant groups disjoint while honoring every premise.', 'Reject a proposed conclusion if that countermodel works.'],\n+    workedExample: { statements: ['Some gardeners are cooks.', 'Some cooks are pilots.'], reasoning: ['Let Ana be a gardener and cook, but not a pilot.', 'Let Bo be a cook and pilot, but not a gardener.', 'Both premises hold without any gardener-pilot overlap.'], conclusion: 'Some gardeners are pilots is not guaranteed.' },\n+    commonMistake: { mistake: 'Using a shared middle word as if it guaranteed a shared middle member.', repair: 'Name different witnesses. If the premises allow them, the chain cannot guarantee overlap.' },\n+    guided: ['All poets are readers. Some readers are swimmers. Must some poet swim?', 'No; the reader-swimmers may be outside the poet group.', 'Yes; all followed by some always links.', 'No poet can swim.', 'The reader-swimming witness need not be a poet. Swimming poets remain possible but unproved.', 'Place the witness outside the narrower class.'],\n+    practice: [\n+      ['Some artists are bakers. Some bakers are divers. What is guaranteed about artist-diver overlap?', 'Nothing; overlap and no overlap are both possible.', 'Some artists are divers.', 'No artists are divers.', 'Different bakers can witness each premise. Neither overlap nor exclusion is forced.', 'Try two different baker witnesses.'],\n+      ['All editors read. Some readers cycle. Must some editor cycle?', 'No.', 'Yes.', 'Every editor cycles.', 'The cycling readers can be noneditors. The universal rule does not place that witness inside editors.', 'An all arrow does not run backward from a some witness.'],\n+      ['Most chefs are gardeners. Must most gardeners be chefs?', 'No.', 'Yes.', 'No gardener is a chef.', 'A majority of chefs may occupy only a small portion of a much larger gardener population.', 'Change the denominator and see what happens.'],\n+      ['Most of ten A are B. B has one hundred members, sixty of whom are C. Must any A be C?', 'No; the A-B members can fit among the forty non-C B members.', 'Yes; two most statements always chain.', 'Most A must be C.', 'The six or more A-B members can all be outside C. The second majority has a different reference group.', 'Use the forty available non-C slots.'],\n+      ['Some guides have radios. All radio owners are trained. Which tempting conclusion goes beyond the premises?', 'All guides are trained.', 'Some guides are trained.', 'Some trained people are guides.', 'The radio-guide witness is trained, giving reversible some overlap. Other guides remain unrestricted.', 'Keep the valid witness conclusion weaker than all.'],\n+      ['All rescue boats have radios. Most radio-equipped boats are inspected. Must most rescue boats be inspected?', 'No.', 'Yes.', 'No rescue boat is inspected.', 'Rescue boats could sit entirely in the minority of radio-equipped boats that are uninspected.', 'Place the narrower set inside the majority population’s minority.'],\n+      ['Most of ten students read. Most of the same ten run. Which conclusion can fail?', 'Most students both read and run.', 'Some students both read and run.', 'At least one student reads.', 'Two six-member majorities may overlap in only two, which is not most of ten. Some overlap is still guaranteed.', 'Compute the smallest overlap, then compare it with half.'],\n+      ['Some designers are licensed. Most licensed people are insured. Must some designer be insured?', 'No; the licensed designers may belong to the uninsured minority.', 'Yes; most includes some, so the witnesses must match.', 'Every designer is uninsured.', 'The designer-licensed witness may be outside the insured majority. Neither universal coverage nor a shared witness is given.', 'Put the existing witness in the majority’s excluded portion.'],\n+      ['Most reviewers are editors. Most editors are translators. Some translators are pilots. Which conclusion is guaranteed?', 'No reviewer-pilot overlap is guaranteed.', 'Some reviewers are pilots.', 'Most reviewers are pilots.', 'Each partial relation may concern different members. Neither most/most across different populations nor the final some supplies a universal bridge.', 'Construct separate witnesses and check each population independently.'],\n+    ],\n+  }),\n+];\n*** End Patch"));

It permits one, several or all. Most means more than half of the stated population. All means every member satisfies the claim, but a universal statement alone does not establish that the population has members.\', \'Keep the reference population fixed.
